links.outcome: Readability (FKGL, FRE) of LLM CKD responses with structured plain-language prompt vs unstructured prompt
links.effect: Structured prompt lowered FKGL from 11.34 to 7.87 (ChatGPT) and 9.62 to 7.13 (Gemini); FRE rose to 64.23 and 61.45; p < 0.001.
links.quote: Providing a structured prompt made the responses of both models significantly easier to read and reduced the required educational level to below high school (7th grade level).

links.outcome: Reading grade level of AI patient education responses with reading-level-targeted prompt vs default
links.effect: Prompt specifying elementary-school comprehension reduced FKGL by over 3 grade levels to about 7th grade; unstructured ChatGPT was 11.34 (high school senior).
links.quote: The reduction in FKGL by over 3 grade levels underscores prompt engineering’s potential as a low-cost intervention to enhance health accessibility.

links.outcome: LLM answer readability above patient literacy, and content quality of responses for patient education
links.effect: Unstructured ChatGPT responses were at FKGL 11.34 (FRE 36.17) and Gemini 9.62, above typical low-literacy levels, though experts scored AI content quality higher than guidelines.
links.quote: In contrast, ChatGPT-4o mini’s responses were at the level of a high school senior and posed greater comprehension challenges.

links.outcome: Blinded expert CLEAR scores of LLM CKD answers versus guideline reference answers
links.effect: Total median: ChatGPT 21.0, Gemini 17.0, Guideline 13.0 (p<0.001); lack of false knowledge ChatGPT and Gemini both 4 vs guideline 3; ICC 0.55.
links.quote: The Kruskal-Wallis test revealed a statistically significant difference in total scores between the three groups (H = 103.49, p < 0.001) (Fig. 2 ).

unlisted_practices: Structured prompt engineering (persona, task, context, format) to improve LLM output readability and quality

links.outcome: readability of AI patient education responses
links.effect: Structured prompt vs unstructured: ChatGPT FKGL 11.34 to 7.87, FRE 36.17 to 64.23; Gemini FKGL 9.62 to 7.13, FRE 46.36 to 61.45; p < 0.001.
links.quote: Compared to unstructured prompt, the use of a structured prompt significantly improved the readability of responses and reduced their complexity for both ChatGPT-4o mini and Gemini (Fig. 3 ).

links.effect: FKGL fell below high school: ChatGPT 11.34 ± 1.79 to 7.87 ± 1.13; Gemini 9.62 ± 1.55 to 7.13 ± 1.78; p < 0.001.
links.quote: Providing a structured prompt made the responses of both models significantly easier to read and reduced the required educational level to below high school (7th grade level).

links.effect: Total-score ICC was 0.55, indicating moderate inter-rater agreement among evaluators.
links.quote: The ICC value was 0.55, indicating moderate agreement among the evaluators.

links.effect: Each prompt ran in two independent sessions; qualitative review found semantic consistency and no significant medical-accuracy or core-recommendation deviations.
links.quote: Upon qualitative review confirming that semantic consistency was maintained across sessions without significant deviations in medical accuracy or core recommendations, the dataset from the first session was retained for the primary analysis.

unlisted_practices: Structured prompt engineering using persona, task, patient context, and elementary-school language format to improve LLM response readability.

links.outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education responses
links.effect: ChatGPT-4o mini responses had FKGL 11.34 and FRE 36.17, requiring high school senior comprehension, significantly less readable than guideline responses (FKGL 9.40, FRE 52.01; p < 0.001).
links.quote: Initial readability analysis showed that guideline responses were easier to comprehend (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL): 9.40; Flesch Reading Ease (FRE): 52.01) than AI-generated content (ChatGPT FKGL: 11.34, FRE: 36.17; Gemini FKGL: 9.62, FRE: 46.36).

unlisted_practices: Structured prompt engineering specifying target reading level to improve readability and reduce reading grade level of AI-generated patient education materials
